newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty finds notch just below resistance.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty finds notch just below resistance.

text.p: The Polish zloty found a comfort zone just below central bank-enforced resistance at 1.5 percent above the parity rate and dealers said that it should remain locked at present levels for days to come.

On Thursday the zloty closed at 1.50/1.47 percent from the trading band centre, a touch weaker from Wednesday's 1.52/1.48 percent, after a languid day spent following dollar/mark moves and some speculative trading late in the session.
Dealers said foreigners, who bought $60 million of Polish bonds at yesterday's tender, would sell currencies in small amounts over the next few days to minimize zloty volatility.

"A small part of foreign purchases of fixed bonds went through the foreign exchange market on Thursday without much effect...and the zloty should be stable in the days to come," said Tomasz Nowakowski, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 3.2276/86 to the dollar on Thursday, down from 3.2260/70 on Wednesday and at 1.8675/80 to the mark, also down from 1.8643/53.

Dealers said some foreigners were selling short-term zloty paper in secondary trade to free up funds and purchase the attractive 15-percent two-year fixed bonds, sold with an average yield of 21.15 percent at yesterday's tender.
"Some foreign investors are selling shorter-term Polish treasuries and buying two-year bonds to omit forex transactions altogether," said Piotr Bednarek, dealer at Warsaw's ING Bank.

Overnight rates eased to close at 22.00/22.10 percent, down 0.20 point at offer, and tomorrow/next deposits closed virtually unchanged at 22.00/22.25 percent as the money market remained liquid despite small demand at Thursday's drainage.
Polish banks bid to place only 50 million zlotys at the central bank's 500 million reverse repo, which dealers said signalled that the market did not have a lot of surplus cash.
Dealers said banks were more interested in building up reserves than placing cash in reverse repos, especially because 14-day deposits were available at higher rates on the market.
At Thursday's 14-day drainage the maximum accepted rate held flat at 22.15 percent while two-week depos were traded around 22.20.
